analysis: This PR adds only documentation: a changelog entry (changelog.d/picker-serving-set-reserve.md) and a new paragraph in docs/architecture/scheduling.md (hunk @@ -47,6 +47,14 @@, after the shared-host memory admission section). No source code is in the batch, so the actual picker change (Start.pickerSelectionFitsBudget in StartCommand+Picker.swift) was not available for review. The docs say the ordinary catalog picker now uses the selected serving set's activation floor within the nominal unified cap, checks each load estimate separately so models can take turns, and does not sample live availability. They also say it does not replace the configured-reserve, outstanding-load or post-load serviceability gates, and that the conservative Autopilot enrollment check and runtime memory safeguards are preserved. The picker is a local provider-side UX check, not an authentication, attestation, encryption, billing or revocation boundary, so it has no direct bearing on TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, T-052..T-058, or the T-041 cache findings. The security-relevant claim for a follow-up pass is that runtime gates remain authoritative: ModelLoadAdmission and EngineV2Reslice.resliceMeetsServiceabilityFloor must still enforce admission, so a looser picker cannot cause overcommit. That is availability or memory-safety only (T-016/T-029 adjacent), not confidentiality. I found no threat-model gap or invalidated assumption from the text alone. needs_deeper_review is false for these doc changes; the accompanying Swift change should be reviewed separately if supplied.
